back: Product vision → product roadmap → release plan → iteration plan → tasks.
A high-level timeline, typically 3 to 6 months, setting the number of iterations and which features come when.
The anticipated sequence of deliverables over time; the product owner replans it as the team delivers.
Enough to understand the first release in broad strokes, and enough items for the next iteration.
A unit of relative effort or complexity for a user story; specific to the team.
Teams compare items better than they predict time; fast; not read as a firm commitment.
XS to XXL, often mapped to 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13.
Items placed on a wall from smaller to larger; good for estimating many items quickly.
Private cards, revealed together; lowest and highest explain; re-vote until the estimates converge.
Story points of the stories accepted in an iteration; team-specific; normalizes over several iterations.
Comparing or ranking teams, treating points as interchangeable, or making velocity a target.
Remaining story points ÷ average velocity = iterations needed (rounded up).
When people are away, the team plans only for the work its reduced capacity allows.
The team agrees what it can complete; lower-priority stories go back to the backlog until it can commit.
1 to 4 weeks, kept the same to establish a cadence.
Prepares upcoming stories, often mid-iteration; aim for no more than about 1 hour a week.
Timeboxed to 15 minutes. Iteration-based: three questions. Flow-based: walk the board right to left.
Work remaining against the time left in a timebox.
Work completed rising toward a total-scope line; added scope shows as that line moving up.
Items finished per time period; stable throughput allows statistical forecasts.
Cycle time: from start of work to finish. Lead time: from the request to delivery.
Items waiting in each workflow state; growing queues signal bottlenecks.
Green outside, red inside: surrogate status like percent done hides problems until late.
Scrum board: cleared each iteration. Kanban board: WIP limits per column, keeps flowing.
PV: points planned to a date. EV: points of stories done. AC: the team's cost.
